9	/-!
10	# DAT-J step 3 is one compatibility square, not a construction
11	
12	`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean` reduced DAT-J to two inputs: a
13	`PicRepDatum k k C` and, for every point `y` of the representing object, a lift
14	
15	> `∃ q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g, q ≫ abel = fromSpecResidueField y`.
16	
17	The lift has been read as "the Abel map is surjective on points", i.e. as geometry still
18	to be done. **The morphism half is already built**, in a rooted file, and what is missing
19	is only that it sits over the right point.
20	
21	## What is landed, and had no consumer
22	
23	`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean` (rooted, sorry-free) carries the whole *fibrewise*
24	chain, and the reason it is short is that **over a field the certificate is free**:
25	
26	* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg` (`:104`) — over a field `K`, an adaptation whose
27	  presentation divisor has degree `n` is `IsCertified n`.  All seven clauses: projectivity
28	  and both flat-cokernel clauses are `Module.Free.of_divisionRing` instances, `(c1)`
29	  finiteness is `moduleFinite_colength`, and the `(c2)` rank clause is the *unconditional*
30	  CRT identity `deg_presentationDivisor` read against the degree hypothesis.  No support
31	  separation is needed — which the file records as a deviation of record, since full
32	  support separation is unachievable when a support point lies in both charts' overlap.
33	* `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq` (`:147`) — hence every effective degree-`g` divisor over
34	  `K` *is* the divisor of a `DivFam`.
35	* `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` (`:217`) — and it classifies, giving
36	  `overSpec k K ⟶ divSchemeOver …`, characterized by `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec`
37	  (`:231`).
38	
39	This is the sharp form of critical-path §7.6's own observation that the `DivFamZar` no-go
40	is a purely *relative* phenomenon, **vacuous over a field**: the difficulty that makes U2
41	hard does not exist fibrewise.
42	
43	## What is therefore actually missing
44	
45	`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec` says the morphism is `divRepClassifyZar` of a family
46	presenting `D`.  It says **nothing about `abel`**.  So joining it to `hlift` needs exactly
47	one statement — that classifying an effective divisor and then applying the Abel map
48	returns the class of that divisor's point:
49	
50	> `AbelCompatible abel` : for every field point and every effective degree-`g` divisor `D`
51	> over it, `(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar … D …).left ≫ abel` is the morphism `Spec K ⟶ J`
52	> named by the class of `D`.
53	
54	That is a *compatibility square*, not a surjectivity theorem, and it is the recorded
55	"groups agree ≠ maps agree" gap (inbox `I-0525`): a bijection between divisor classes and
56	`DivScheme`-points is unusable until the square relating the two named morphisms lands.
57	
58	## Main declarations
59	
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelClassifyCompatible` — the square, as a named interface.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` — the square plus
62	  fibrewise effectivity gives the `hlift` obligation **verbatim** as
63	  `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` / `PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` consume it.
64	
65	## What this does NOT do
66	
67	It produces no `AbelClassifyCompatible` and no effectivity witness, so it builds no
68	`JacobianData`.  It removes the *construction* from DAT-J step 3 and leaves a square and
69	an effectivity input, both stated here rather than assumed anywhere.
70	-/

119	
120	/-- **The Abel-compatibility square** — the one statement standing between the landed
121	fibrewise classification and DAT-J's `hlift` obligation.
122	
123	At a scheme `J` and a morphism `abel : DivScheme g ⟶ J`, this says: whenever a point `y`
124	of `J` is presented by an effective degree-`g` divisor `D` on the curve over its own
125	residue field — presented in the sense that the classifying morphism composed with `abel`
126	is required to be `fromSpecResidueField y` — the composite is that structural morphism.
127	
128	Stated as a hypothesis over `y` and `D` rather than as a surjectivity claim, because that
129	is the shape `hlift` consumes: `hlift` needs, *for each* `y`, *some* divisor; the geometric
130	content is producing `D`, and the bookkeeping content is this square.  Separating them is
131	the point of this file (compare inbox `I-0525`: an isomorphism of class groups is unusable
132	without the square relating the named morphisms). -/
133	def IsAbelClassifyCompatible {J : Scheme.{u}} (abel : DivSch ⟶ J)
134	    (pt : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
135	      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
136	      [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))],
137	      (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor → (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ J)) : Prop :=
138	  ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
139	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
140	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
141	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
142	    (D : (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor) (hD : 0 ≤ D)
143	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ)),
144	    (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D hD hdeg).left ≫ abel
145	      = pt K D
146	
147	/-- **The `hlift` obligation from the square plus fibrewise effectivity** — `DAT-J` step 3
148	in the exact shape `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
149	`PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` consume (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean`,
150	`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean`).
151	
152	The lift is `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` of the supplied divisor, and the triangle is the
153	square.  Note what is *not* here: no surjectivity of the Abel map on points is proved, and
154	no divisor is produced — `heff` is the honest geometric input (Riemann–Roch: a degree-`g`
155	class on a curve of genus `g` over a field has an effective representative, to be spelled
156	with `exists_effective_of_picClass` / `riemann_inequality` and **never** with
157	`riemann_inequality_curve`, which imports `Challenge.lean`). -/
158	theorem exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible {J : Scheme.{u}} (abel : DivSch ⟶ J)
159	    (pt : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
160	      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
161	      [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))],
162	      (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor → (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ J))
163	    (hsq : IsAbelClassifyCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 abel pt)
164	    (heff : ∀ y : J, ∃ (_ : Algebra k (J.residueField y))
165	      (_ : IsIntegral (relCurve C (J.residueField y)))
166	      (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
167	        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
168	      (_ : QuasiCompact
169	        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
170	      (D : (relCurve C (J.residueField y)).CurveDivisor) (_ : 0 ≤ D)
171	      (_ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg (J.residueField y) D = (g : ℤ)),
172	      pt (J.residueField y) D = J.fromSpecResidueField y) :
173	    ∀ y : J, ∃ q : Spec (J.residueField y) ⟶ DivSch,
174	      q ≫ abel = J.fromSpecResidueField y := by
175	  intro y
176	  obtain ⟨_, _, _, _, D, hD, hdeg, hpt⟩ := heff y
177	  exact ⟨(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D hD hdeg).left,
178	    (hsq (J.residueField y) D hD hdeg).trans hpt⟩
179	
180	end AbelSquare

8	/-!
9	# DJ-1, the topological half: point surjectivity from residue-field lifts
10	
11	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean` reduced DAT-J's quasi-compactness field to a single
12	statement, `Function.Surjective abel.base` — *step 3* of `informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
13	§2.2, the node's one honest brick.  §2.3 describes the argument for it in the language the
14	Picard theory supplies: *every field point of `J.left` is a degree-zero class over its
15	residue field, shift it by `fiberTwist`, take an effective representative, and that
16	representative is a `DivScheme`-point hitting the original point.*
17	
18	That argument produces, for a point `y`, a **morphism** `Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g` — not an
19	element of the fibre of `abel.base` over `y`.  Nothing in the tree converted the first into
20	the second, and it is not bookkeeping that can be skipped: the target of DJ-1 is a statement
21	about the underlying *topological* map, while everything the Picard side produces is a
22	morphism of schemes.
23	
24	This file supplies exactly that conversion, and nothing else:
25	
26	> `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — if for every `y : Y` some
27	> `q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X` satisfies `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then
28	> `f.base` is surjective.
29	
30	The proof is `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField` (mathlib): the range of
31	`Y.fromSpecResidueField y` is `{y}`, and `Spec κ(y)` is nonempty because `κ(y)` is a field,
32	so any point of `Spec κ(y)` maps into the fibre.  Composed with the DJ-0 lemmas this gives
33	the Jacobian datum producers in the shape the classical argument actually delivers: a
34	*per-point lift*, which is what `exists_effective_of_picClass` hands back.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — the conversion.
39	  Pure scheme topology; no curve, no Picard functor, no divisor scheme.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme` — DJ-1's qc
41	  step from per-point lifts.
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
43	  `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` — the two `JacobianData` producers
44	  with the surjectivity hypothesis replaced by per-point lifts.
45	
46	## What this does NOT do
47	
48	It produces no lift.  Producing one is the divRep-gated mathematics of §2.3 (the
49	`fiberTwist` shift plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`, which must stay Challenge-free per
50	§0.5 — `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`).  What changes is the shape
51	of that obligation: a lift *per point*, stated with no reference to `Function.Surjective`,
52	instead of a global surjectivity claim about a topological map.
53	-/

70	/-- **Per-point residue-field lifts give point surjectivity.**  If every point `y` of `Y`
71	admits a morphism `q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ X` with `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then the
72	underlying map of `f` is surjective.
73	
74	`Spec κ(y)` is nonempty (a field is nontrivial), and the range of `Y.fromSpecResidueField y`
75	is `{y}` (mathlib `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField`), so the image under `q` of any point
76	of `Spec κ(y)` lies in the fibre of `f` over `y`.
77	
78	This is the missing link between what the Picard side produces and what DAT-J's
79	quasi-compactness field consumes: `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields a *morphism* out of
80	a residue field, while `quasiCompact_of_surjective` wants a surjection of topological
81	spaces. -/
82	theorem surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift (f : X ⟶ Y)
83	    (h : ∀ y : Y, ∃ q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X,
84	      q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y) :
85	    Function.Surjective f.base := by
86	  intro y
87	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := h y
88	  -- a field is nontrivial, so `Spec κ(y)` has a point
89	  obtain ⟨s⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (Y.residueField y)))
90	  refine ⟨q.base s, ?_⟩
91	  have hs : (q ≫ f).base s = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base s := by rw [hq]
92	  rw [Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply] at hs
93	  exact hs
94	
95	end Topology

## DAT-J residues, measured

**A. The interface** (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquare.lean`, 183 lines, **sorry-free as a term** — the one `grep` hit is docstring prose at :23; rooted at `AlgebraicJacobian.lean:607`).

`IsAbelClassifyCompatible` (:133) takes `abel : DivSch ⟶ J` **plus a second parameter `pt`**, a function `∀ (K) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)] [Smooth…] [QuasiCompact…], (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor → (Spec (.of K) ⟶ J)`, and asserts `∀ K … (D) (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hdeg : deg K D = g), (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D hD hdeg).left ≫ abel = pt K D`.

**This is the finding: `pt` is universally quantified in the theorem, not pinned.** I proved in Lean (axiom-clean, `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`) that for **any** `J` and **any** `abel`, `∃ pt, IsAbelClassifyCompatible … abel pt` — witness `fun K … D => if h : 0 ≤ D ∧ deg K D = g then (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar … D h.1 h.2).left ≫ abel else fallback K`, closed by `dif_pos`. And the converse: `hlift` plus bare existence of an effective degree-`g` divisor per residue field reconstructs `pt`, `hsq` **and** `heff`, with the `hlift` binder reported *unused* by the linter.

So `exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` is an **equivalence, not a reduction**. All content sits in `heff`, whose real conjunct is not `pt K D = fromSpecResidueField y` in the abstract but `(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar … D …).left ≫ abel = J.fromSpecResidueField y` — i.e. the square *at the residue-field points*, restated. The docstring's "the bookkeeping content is this square" inverts the actual split. Obligation 1 as stated is discharged by `probe_square_vacuous`; it demands nothing.

**B. Effectivity.** `exists_effective_of_picClass` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:208`):
```lean
lemma exists_effective_of_picClass (W : X.CurveDivisor)
    (hW : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K)) :
    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K W
```
`riemann_inequality` (`RiemannRoch/ChiLedger.lean:137`, **not** FLVClass:205): `deg K D + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ)`.

The **degree arithmetic is genuinely free** — I proved it: from `deg W = g` and `chi = 1 - g`, `hW` is `omega`, and the returned `E` has `deg E = g` via `classDeg_picClass` (`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean:157`). No `g`-vs-`n` shift.

Three real gaps, all confirmed by failed `infer_instance`:
- **`Algebra k (J.residueField y)` does not synthesise**, even for `J.Over (Spec (.of k))`. Mathlib's `ResidueField.lean` has no such instance (only `Hom.residueFieldMap`, :123, and `FormallyUnramified.lean:157`'s local `letI … .hom.toAlgebra`). This is why `heff` bundles it as *data* — correctly. The missing construction is `(J ↘ Spec (.of k)).residueFieldMap y` composed with the affine `Γ`-identification.
- **relCurve-alias keying**: `IsIntegral (relCurve C K)`, both `Module.Finite … HModule 0/1`, `Smooth`, `QuasiCompact` all fail at the alias but succeed at `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`, and `relCurve C K = (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` is `rfl`. `DivSchemeAbel.lean:280-288` works around this with explicit `haveI`s naming `instIsIntegralBaseChange` etc. (`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean:152/167/176`).
- **`chi` at the residue field** is `chi_relCurve_baseField` (`DivSchemeSeedUnivAssembleKappa.lean:68`); available, needs the `Algebra` datum first.

**C. There is no campaign `abel`.** Grep for anything whose *type produces* `DivScheme … ⟶ J`: every occurrence is a **hypothesis** (`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:79,107,117,146`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:120,152`, `JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:133`). The only constructed `DivScheme`-source morphism is `divSchemeι : DivScheme … ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂` (`DivScheme.lean:148`), wrong target. `DivSchemeAbel.lean` builds the Abel map only as a **natural transformation** `abelDivTrans : divFunctor C π n ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C n` (:302), and `abelSigmaChart` (`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:205`) turns it into a presheaf map — both need `(divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D`, i.e. **divRep**. So "prove `IsAbelClassifyCompatible` for the campaign's Abel morphism" has no subject: the scheme-level `abel` is itself divRep-gated. `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec` (`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:231`) pins only the *left* side (`= divRepClassifyZar … F.toZar` with `divFamDivisor F = D`); nothing in the tree relates `divRepClassifyZar` to any `abel` — zero grep hits for a composition lemma.

**D. Producers** — `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` (`JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:149`), `ofChartsOfAbelLifts` (:193), `PicRepDatum.toJacobianData` (`JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:83`, four fields, `hqc` the only argument), `toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` (:132). All sorry-free. The conversion `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` (:82) is real, cheap, and complete.

**E. Verdict.** Nothing is *already discharged under another name* (workspace search: AJC's `Scheme.PicScheme.HasAbelMap`/`abelMap` in `FGAPicRepresentability.lean:661` is a different category and sits behind protection I-0074's 4 sorries). Ranking:

2. `heff`'s degree half — already provable (I proved it); needs only (1) plus the alias `haveI`s.
3. `IsAbelClassifyCompatible` — **not a target**: vacuous as stated. It needs restating with `pt` pinned (e.g. via a landed class-to-point morphism) before it means anything, and its honest form is divRep-gated because `abel` does not exist.
